name: remotion-viz
description: Render Remotion videos and rasterize SVG/HTML visualizations, with diagnostics that name the fix for every failure.
long_description:
Gives Claude two capabilities it does not have on its own: the ability to actually run Remotion on your machine, and the ability to see what an SVG or HTML visualization renders to.

**Remotion.** Scaffold a project, list compositions, render stills and video. `remotion_render_still` attaches the rendered PNG to its response, so a layout can be checked in seconds instead of waiting minutes for a full encode.

**Visualization.** `viz_validate_svg` catches the reasons SVG renders blank — malformed XML, HTML-only entities like ` `, a missing `xmlns` or `viewBox`, stripped `<script>` blocks, blocked external references — and returns a specific fix for each. `viz_render_svg` rasterizes to PNG so the result can be inspected rather than assumed.

**Diagnostics.** `remotion_check_environment` reports on Node, the Remotion install, the entry point and the Chrome Headless Shell, with a remedy attached to each failure.

Every file path is confined to the workspace directory you choose during setup, and it is not defaulted - you pick it. No command is run through a shell, tool arguments cannot become CLI flags, rendered SVG cannot read files outside the workspace, and HTML renders with no network access unless you allow specific hosts.

workspace.title: Workspace directory
workspace.description: The single folder that holds your Remotion projects. Every file path the tools accept is resolved against it and cannot escape it, and viz_render_svg can read image files anywhere under it, so choose the narrowest folder that contains your work - not your whole home directory.

chrome_path.title: Chrome executable (optional)
chrome_path.description: Only needed for viz_render_html, and only if auto-detection fails. Leave empty and the extension will look for a system Chrome, Chromium, Edge or Brave, then fall back to the browser Remotion downloads for rendering.

allowed_hosts.title: Allowed network hosts (optional)
allowed_hosts.description: Comma-separated hostnames that viz_render_html may load resources from, e.g. fonts.googleapis.com,fonts.gstatic.com. Empty means no network access while rendering, which is the default. Loopback, private and link-local addresses are always blocked.
